4) Book a follow-up technical deep-dive with our solutions engineer + your infra devs (proposed Fri 7/16).

Alex / Priya —

Following up with the technical details you asked for and a sample policy snippet. Attached the integration guide (redwood-integration-guide.pdf) with code examples; below are quick highlights to unblock your devs.

Auth & SDK setup:
- Sandbox: we can issue a static API key for testing. For prod we support short-lived JWTs (via OIDC) and mTLS for Dedicated/Private installs. mTLS is supported at the gRPC endpoint; for REST we recommend JWT + mutual TLS on the network when using Private deployment.
- Sample header (REST):
  Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TEST_TOKEN>
  X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp-id
- SDKs: node/python snippets in the attached PDF. Example (node):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });

Model routing & policy (concepts):
- Two important knobs: latency_slo_ms and cost_preference (prefer_latency | balance_cost | prefer_cost).
- Fallback chain: ordered list of compatible model families. When latency_slo_ms is violated we attempt the next model in the chain. Important: KV cache is model-family-aware; using compatible variants (same architecture) preserves cache hits.

Sample policy (drop-in):
{
  "policy_name": "acme-interactive-1",
  "latency_slo_ms": "120",
  "cost_preference": "prefer_latency",
  "fallback_chain": ["redwood/turbo-v2", "redwood/medium-v1", "open/ggml-quant-2"],
  "region_routing": {"primary": "us-west-2", "fallbacks": ["us-east-1"]}
}

Notes on behavior:
- If p95 latency exceeds latency_slo_ms, requests are routed to the next model in fallback_chain for that request or route.
- Cache reuse: if you can pin to a model family (e.g., turbo-v2 variants) you get best KV reuse. Mixed-architecture fallbacks will have lower cache hit rates.
- Cost implications: fallback to quantized ggml variants saves ~3-5x token cost but increases inference CPU usage and might affect latency variability.

Embeddings & reranker:
- Recommended flow:
  1) Use dense embeddings (512-1536 dim depending on model) produced by Redwood embeddings API.
  2) Index with Faiss (or Pinecone) for ANN recall (top 100).
  3) Run a lightweight reranker model (small-turbo reranker) on the top-K (K=10-50) to score and return final results.
- Redwood can host reranker models for you and support a two-call pattern (recall -> rerank) or you can implement reranking in your infra. We recommend hosted reranker to simplify latency and deployment.

Structured output & tool calling:
- Use function/tool calling for product lookup: define a schema for product lookup responses and have the model fill structured fields. Example interface is in the attached guide.
- For high-assurance outputs, enable deterministic sampling + output validation on our side before returning to your service.

Region routing & data residency:
- We support route-by-origin-ip or route-by-request-header. For EU traffic we recommend a separate route with primary eu-west-1 and fallback eu-central-1.

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf (code, policy templates, sample reranker configs).

If it helps I can paste a ready-to-drop policy JSON into your repo or create a sandbox token for priya@acme.com now.
